item.content:encoded:
The thing that made the article interesting for me was the idea that the Insurgency knew more about this seemingly benign object than the Foundation. What is it that they are missing? What do they not know? And most importantly, why does the Insurgency care so much about it?

To that end I kinda wish that it was left a mystery, so that we would always wonder what was so special about this mirror. That said, it is still a very good article, in my opinion.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A) It's got a rather well-done audio log attached to it.

B) It is considerably well-thought out - an item with a very minor effect is given a great deal of detail and backstory, and strength comes from that. See, from what I'm picking up you split the two. The article needs to be looked at as a whole: the mirror, the Insurgency, the history, and the final purpose all combined. Shows that a lot of work and thought went into it, and people tend to appreciate that.

There are no outside memes here.

Also, it's okay not to like things. Not voting on something because you don't care for it that much is in no way connected to the end of the world as we know it, surprisingly enough.

item.content:encoded: I may just be missing the point here, but I don't understand why this article is so highly rated. The SCP itself is "meh" and the tale is just kind of interesting. It's likely that there are allusions to things I've never even heard of that make this good, but as an introverted, culturally-abstained, simple-minded twenty-year-old who has never heard of any but the absolute most common memes anywhere ever and is incapable of picking up on the kinds of subtleties that are needed to solve a riddle, this is not an interesting article to me. The only reason I'd downvote it is because I feel like it has too many upvotes (which I'm pretty sure would qualify as malicious downvoting), but I can't upvote it because it's really not that great in my opinion - and I'm pretty generous with my upvotes.

item.title: Doubt
item.content:encoded:
When I first saw this featured on the front page, I was doubtful as to whether I've already read it or not, but I was pretty sure I had at least seen it a year prior. When I saw it featured, I thought the "addition" of the "long term effect" was pretty awesome because I wasn't sure if I had already read the article.

Maybe another year or so later I am now doubtful if that was actually an addition, or if the long term effect had always been part of the article. Perhaps the earliest version disappeared from the history? I don't know. Maybe it was always there and I just forgot. People have reassured me it's always been that way. But I'm almost certain it was at first only an SCP about a mirror that causes razor mis-usage.

All in all, the article's been highly nostalgic two times so far.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The twentieth.

One of the things I attempted to do with this SCP was have it actually show a real progression of time and events over an extended period, to the point of subtly varying writing styles and sentence formation over "time" in an attempt to reflect the object's care changing hands, newer people coming along, etc. The person writing this sentence was born in the 19th Century, writing sometime in the 1940's or 50's, and he had some of the writing mannerisms common from that shift (referring to the passing of time in new/old century, for example). For that reason, I'm not going to edit the article to clarify this particular problem, as I feel that you've perfectly picked up on the clue I was attempting to convey in the exact manner I was hoping for: How long have we been dealing with this thing and what exactly is its scope?

Thanks for the careful reading, though! It's extremely gratifying to know that someone picked up on this clue.
